comments.content: The pair is only honoured when both values are non-`Color.Unspecified` (`overrideColorsGiven` in `MangaButton`, `overrideColors` in `ClassicButton`). Because both parameters are individually optional with the same sentinel default, a caller that supplies only one of them gets the themed colour back with no compile-time or runtime signal — the button simply renders differently from what was requested (e.g. the destructive label keeps the accent colour instead of the fixed error colour). This is duplicated in two places, so the two conditions can also drift apart. Consider making the pairing explicit, e.g. take a single nullable `ButtonColors`/colour-pair parameter, or add a debug-only `check` that fails loudly on a partial pair.

`movedBackToOlder` compares the *installed* version against `newTag`, but the value written is `snapshotLatestVersion` (`app.latestVersion`), without verifying it is actually ahead of `newTag`. `updateAppVersion` never refreshes `latestVersion`, so the DB can legitimately hold `installedVersion` > `latestVersion` (e.g. installed 2.1 installed from Details while the tracked latest is still 2.0). In that state a downgrade to 2.0 records `skippedReleaseTag = "2.0"` — the release that was just installed — which then shows up in the skipped-updates UI and is not cleared by `checkForUpdates` until a strictly newer release appears.

comments.content: `isUpdate` is not only consumed by `validateApk`; it is threaded through `installAsset` → `saveInstalledAppToDatabase`, where it selects `updateInstalledAppVersion` instead of `saveNewInstalledApp`. So switching this from `false` to `installedApp != null` also changes the persistence path for reinstalls/downgrades: `saveNewInstalledApp` is what refreshes the picked-asset metadata (`preferredAssetVariant`, `preferredAssetTokens`, `assetGlobPattern`, `pickedAssetIndex`, sibling count) via `AssetVariant.fingerprintFromPickedAsset`. With this change, a user who picks a different asset variant in `ReleaseAssetsPicker` and installs it over an existing install keeps the old variant preference, so later update checks keep resolving the previously pinned asset. If that side effect isn't intended, consider gating only the package-mismatch check on a dedicated flag rather than reusing `isUpdate`.

comments.content:
This rewrite does not actually require the older build to be on the device. `updateAppVersion` is also called for installs that have not completed: `InstallationManagerImpl.updateInstalledAppVersion` is invoked from `saveInstalledAppToDatabase` with `isPendingInstall = true` for any non-COMPLETED outcome (and the interface default is `isPendingInstall = true`). On the default Android path (`AndroidInstaller.install` returns `DELEGATED_TO_SYSTEM` right after `startActivity`), the orchestrator emits `Completed` immediately, so this runs as soon as the APK is handed to the system installer.

Consequence: if the user cancels (or Android rejects) the install of the older build, `skippedReleaseTag` has already been set to the previous `latestVersion`, and nothing clears it — `checkForUpdates` then hits `matchesSkipped` and stops offering that release, even though the device is still running it. Consider recording the skip only once the older build is confirmed (e.g. where the pending install is resolved with `systemInfo`), or clearing a skip that was written by an install that never landed.
